alex: Heads-up: node gpu-rack-12-node07 is spiking Xid 13 and 17, and ECC counters incremented after two short runs. Repro'd on obvious load. Thinking we should follow a burn-in + soak workflow before returning to service. Anyone have a concise checklist?

maria: Yep — good call. Quick checklist I use: cordon/drain -> isolate -> burn-in script loop (memtest+stress+cuda) -> monitor nvml/dmesg/Xid -> soak 24-72h -> pass/fail criteria. Details below. :white_check_mark:

ryan: Add a hardware isolation step first: reseat GPU, swap riser, try on known-good PSU; if still flaky move to bench and run extended tests. If it goes away on swap, it's likely riser or slot/os power.

alex: @infra-bot can you cordon/drain the node so we don't schedule more workloads?

infra-bot: cordon: kubectl cordon gpu-rack-12-node07 (done)
infra-bot: drain: kubectl drain gpu-rack-12-node07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data (done)

maria: For software tests, I use these checks in order:
- nvml query for ECC and Xid history: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.errors.corrected.volatile.total,ecc.errors.uncorrected.volatile.total --format=csv`
- tail dmesg | grep -i nvidia and look for Xid codes (13/17/65 most common for memory/cpu?wd)
- run cuda_memtest or memtest for GPUs: https://github.com/whmiller/cuda_memtest or vendor tool
- stress CPU + sustained GPU kernels to force HV/temps: stress-ng + a CUDA loop

maria: Share a tiny burn-in loop I run on bench machines:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# burnin.sh - loop memtest and stress for quick soak
LOGDIR=/tmp/gpu-burnin-logs
mkdir -p $LOGDIR
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do
  echo "=== ITER $i $(date) ===" | tee -a $LOGDIR/burnin.log
  # run GPU memtest (replace with compiled cuda_memtest binary)
  ./cuda_memtest --iterations 100 --timeout 300 2>&1 | tee -a $LOGDIR/memtest.$i.log
  # run a few minutes of sustained kernels (example: cudabench or a simple looping kernel)
  python3 gpu_stress.py --seconds 300 2>&1 | tee -a $LOGDIR/stress.$i.log
  # sample nvml + dmesg
  nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu,driver_model.current,ecc.errors.uncorrected.volatile.total --format=csv >> $LOGDIR/nvml.$i.csv
  dmesg | tail -n 200 | grep -i nvidia >> $LOGDIR/dmesg.$i.log || true
  sleep 10
done
```

maria: If you want a faster confidence metric, run 10-20 iterations and require zero new uncorrected ECC errors and zero Xid events in dmesg. For return-to-service policy we require: either 72 hours of continuous soak with no new Xid/ECC (preferred) OR 1000 iterations of the memtest loop with zero uncorrected ECC + no driver TDRs.

ryan: Important: count severity. Small increments of corrected ECC may be tolerated but any uncorrected ECC increment -> FAIL and request RMA. Also annotate machine in inventory: tag `flaky-gpu` + add notes about exchanged riser/PSU.

alex: If hardware isolation passes (no errors after reseating and bench test), do we still require the full 72h soak before uncordon?

maria: Yes, at least 24h for staging clusters, 72h for prod. If we swapped components (riser/PSU) then keep node quarantined longer and run soak in bench or isolated rack. Document results in the node ticket.

oncall-sre: Also add monitoring hooks: create a short-lived Grafana panel for GPU ECC/unccd Xid events with 1m resolution and alert if any uncorrected ECC > 0 or Xid count increases. We can auto-fail the soak if alert fires.

alex: Sounds good. Plan: 1) reseat & swap riser/PSU 2) run 10 quick memtest iterations on bench 3) if clean, start 72h soak on isolated capacity with nvml/dmesg monitoring 4) uncordon after passing criteria. I'll create a ticket and tag node.

maria: If soak fails mid-run, capture full logs and we escalate to RMA. Also helpful to record ambient temps and power draw. Flaky GPUs often correlate with thermal cycling.

ryan: One more gotcha: driver/kernel combos can cause spurious Xid codes. If hardware checks out, repro on a different kernel/driver before RMA. If it only reproduces on our specific kernel, file a bug with the driver/vendor.

alex: Thanks — I'll start now and paste the burn-in logs into the ticket.

infra-bot: ticket created: INF-6721 - gpu-rack-12-node07 burn-in + soak

maria: Copy this thread into the ticket as the runbook snippet. We should cross-post a condensed runbook to the eng-infra runbooks folder after this.

alex: Quick Q: thresholds to auto-fail soak alerts? Propose: any uncorrected ECC inc -> immediate fail; Xid >= 1 in 24h -> fail; more than 3 corrected ECC increments/hour -> flag for extended soak.

oncall-sre: Agreed. I'll add those to alert rules.

ryan: If anyone takes the node to bench and wants me to witness the swap, ping me and I'll come by.

alex: Thanks all. I'll update ticket INF-6721 with logs and next steps.

(most messages short/concise per usual Slack style)
